result:
Looking at this evidence against the specific claim ("accessible to screen reader users"), there's a real gap: nothing here actually tests with a screen reader. Here's the row.

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| **Claim** | New checkout flow is accessible to screen reader users. |
| **Status** | Not substantiated as stated — evidence supports a narrower claim than the one written. |
| **Evidence** | (1) axe-core CI scan, 0 violations. (2) Designer (Dana) sighted walkthrough, confirms visual/structural match to existing accessible component library. (3) Same component set shipped on account settings page last month, no reported issues. (4) Change scope: swap-in of existing components, no new custom UI. |
| **Gap** | No one has actually driven the checkout flow with a screen reader (NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver). axe-core is a static/DOM linter — it catches missing labels, contrast, ARIA misuse, etc., but not focus management between steps, live-region announcements for validation/loading/error states, reading order vs. visual order, or behavior inside any payment iframe. Dana's review was visual ("looks right"), which doesn't test the non-visual experience the claim is actually about. "No complaints" on account settings is absence of evidence, not evidence — most users don't file accessibility bugs, they just bounce — and that page has a simpler interaction pattern (no multi-step flow, no async payment/error states) than checkout. Component-level accessibility also doesn't guarantee flow-level accessibility; composition bugs are exactly what evade both axe-core and visual QA. |
| **Tests run** | Automated: axe-core, CI-gated, 0 violations. Manual: sighted design review against component library. |
| **Tests not run** | Manual screen reader pass on the critical path (add to cart → checkout → validation errors → payment step → confirmation), across at least one of NVDA/VoiceOver. Keyboard-only navigation test. Live-region/announcement check for async states (loading, error, success). |
| **Non-claims** | This evidence does **not** establish: WCAG 2.1 AA conformance for the flow; usability for actual screen reader users; correct behavior of dynamic/async states (errors, loading, payment processing) under assistive tech; accessibility of any third-party payment iframe if one is embedded. |

**Recommendation:** either (a) run a 30–60 min manual screen reader smoke test on the checkout path before Friday — even just one pass catches most flow-level issues axe-core misses — or (b) if that's not feasible in time, reword the claim to match the evidence you actually have (e.g., "New checkout flow passes automated accessibility scanning and matches our accessible component library; manual screen reader testing pending") and file a follow-up ticket. Shipping the claim as currently worded without a manual pass is the part I'd push back on.
